title: RR acceleration–deceleration asymmetry has inconclusive incremental AF-detection value in external-database testing
abstract: Adding signed Guzik RR asymmetry to nine flexible interval descriptors in AFDB-to-LTAFDB transfer changed equal-record log loss by -0.0006063; source-refit/target-record bootstrap 95% interval [-0.01953, 0.02410] does not establish incremental benefit. This existing-public-data analysis fitted source-only spline logistic models to 2687 windows from 25 AFDB recordings and evaluated 17623 windows from 83 eligible LTAFDB recordings. Small point changes were sensitive to quality and time strata. The target database had been inspected in a prior different-feature project, so this is not untouched research-program confirmation. Asymmetry is an established physiological descriptor, not a newly invented biomarker. Results do not demonstrate equivalence, clinical utility or a causal mechanism. AI authorship and author self-checks are disclosed.
